statement: For the actual boundary quotient and compatible universal-cover lift of C42, the real lifted fibres are connected proper lines and an actual homeomorphism T from R times R onto the covering plane satisfies F(T(u,t))=t. The component partition has genuine local product charts, and the original quotient has local projection charts with its stated target coordinate.
depends_on: C42 compatible transitive Polish group and proper-line components; verified Polish open orbit-map theorem; C33 elementary surface product cancellation; Aarts-Oversteegen 1991 Definition 5.3, Theorems 5.6-5.7, Main Theorem 0.5 and Remark 4.4; Baillif-Gabard 2008 Theorem 1.1
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; actual boundary-quotient maps in the remaining relative centralizer extension
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The compact-open Polish action verifies the exact regularity definition before the flowbox theorem is applied. The quotient topology is proved open, its interval charts are explicitly identified using F, and Lindelofness and homogeneity are established before applying the separation theorem.
notes: Effros openness supplies uniformly close embeddings of every compact component arc through all nearby points. Aarts-Oversteegen gives product neighborhoods, and the C33 product-cancellation proof makes their transverse factors intervals. Openness of F makes the transverse coordinate strictly monotone. The component quotient is open, second countable, homogeneous and locally an interval; Baillif-Gabard makes it Hausdorff. Its local homeomorphism to R is then a global homeomorphism, proving connected fibres. Plane orientation and the F transverse orientation supply a coherent leaf orientation. The auxiliary complete free flow has exactly these leaves; saturating an actual F-section gives a homeomorphism by invariance of domain. Explicit additive transition functions and a locally finite partition of unity give the global product. This flow is not asserted to be operator-equivariant, compatible with other boundary quotient maps, or extendible across the frontier. C12 remains open.
